title: Integral identity and its exact raw rationalization
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the framework integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^s(T)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the PBC integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^p(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category].
Put $R_{E,T}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T$. The identity of the common full integral subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_{E,T}))$ in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] defines an exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear equivalence $I_{T,E}$ between the framework and PBC integral categories, preserving their finite-reduction functors. Its raw rationalization is an exact $E$-linear equivalence
$$J_{T,E}:\mathcal C_E^s(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_E^p(T),\qquad K\longmapsto K,\quad u\otimes x\longmapsto u\otimes x.$$
The inverse has these same formulas. The integral and rational shift comparisons are induced by the identity on the ambient complexes; both equivalences and their inverses preserve distinguished triangles. No objects or retracts are adjoined. In the concrete completed-coefficient presentations, $I_{T,E}$ is restriction along the quotient-normalized coefficient isomorphism, and its rationalization satisfies the integral-object and pure-tensor pins of [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum].

proof.text: Fix $E$ and write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi=\varpi_E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison] to obtain the unique coefficient isomorphism $e_T:B_T^p\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{E,T}$ with $\pi_n^s e_T=\bar e_n\pi_n^p$. Restriction along $e_T$ goes from the framework presentation to the PBC presentation; restriction along $e_T^{-1}$ goes back. These derived equivalences identify all finite reductions and quotient transitions. To restrict their domains, apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]: after this coefficient identification its conditions describe exactly both integral categories, including the PBC compatible etale-origin witnesses. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed noetherian, finite-dimensional $T$ with $\ell$ invertible, and finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Thus the restrictions are defined in both directions. In the common $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_{E,T}))$ realization they are identity on objects and arrows. Call the forward restriction $I_{T,E}$; it preserves the prescribed finite reductions, without choosing an arbitrary equivalence of their targets.

proof.text: The integral shifts and triangles on each side are inherited from the ambient derived categories by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] and [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the exact coefficient restrictions of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison]. It gives triangulated derived functors and shift comparisons induced by degreewise identities: restricting a complex and shifting it gives the same terms and signed differentials as shifting first. Restriction also carries the cone with differential matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ to the cone of the restricted $f$ with that same matrix. It preserves quasi-isomorphisms by exactness. Consequently the identity comparisons descend to the ambient derived categories and preserve their distinguished triangles, and then those in the full integral subcategories, in both directions. By [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear], the $A$-action on the framework Hom groups is the constant-section action. The quotient formula for $e_T$ sends each constant scalar $a$ to that same scalar at every finite quotient, so its inverse does too. The coefficient restrictions therefore commute with the $A$-action on complexes and derived arrows. Hence $I_{T,E}$ and its inverse are exact $A$-linear functors with the stated identity-induced shifts.

proof.text: Use the two raw rationalization definitions [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and their scalar-localization operations [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Define $J_{T,E}(K)=I_{T,E}K$ and $J_{T,E}(f\otimes x)=I_{T,E}(f)\otimes x$. This is balanced: $I(af)\otimes x=aI(f)\otimes x=I(f)\otimes ax$; additivity gives a map on finite sums of pure tensors. It preserves identities because $I(\mathrm{id}_K)\otimes1=\mathrm{id}_{IK}\otimes1$. For composable $f,g$, its value on $(g\otimes y)\circ(f\otimes x)=(gf)\otimes yx$ is $I(g)I(f)\otimes yx$, the composite of their images; bilinearity gives the assertion for arbitrary arrows. Also $J(z(f\otimes x))=I(f)\otimes zx=zJ(f\otimes x)$ for $z\in E$, hence $J$ is $E$-linear. Perform the identical construction with $I^{-1}$. In the common integral realization both composites are identity on objects and pure tensors, hence on all morphisms. In the concrete presentations the unit and counit are the localized restriction round trips, identity on the underlying modules. This proves equivalence and the inverse formulas. In the common realization $I(f)=f$, so these are exactly $K\mapsto K$, $f\otimes x\mapsto f\otimes x$ and the integral-object and tensor pins of [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum]. The definitions retain exactly the integral objects; no retracts are adjoined.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] to the two integral categories: step 2 supplies their $A$-linear shifts. Their rational shifts act by $(f\otimes x)[1]=f[1]\otimes x$, as specified in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Thus the identity-induced integral shift comparison of step 2 localizes to the shift comparison for $J$, and likewise for its inverse. For any distinguished rational triangle $\Delta$, the cited triangulated-localization statement gives a distinguished integral triangle $\Delta_0$ and an isomorphism $\Delta\simeq Q_s\Delta_0$. The formulas of step 3 give $JQ_s=Q_pI$ with these shift comparisons. Step 2 makes $I\Delta_0$ distinguished; the same localization statement makes $Q_pI\Delta_0$ distinguished. Applying $J$ to the displayed isomorphism shows that $J\Delta$ is distinguished. Repeat with $I^{-1}$ and $J^{-1}$ to obtain exactness of the inverse. This proves all rational exactness and shift assertions while retaining the raw categories of step 3.
